note: The qere ba gad means "fortune has come" (gad = luck, also a deity of fortune, Isa 65:11; the ketiv bgd = "with fortune"); the KJV connects Gad with gedud, "troop", as in 49:19.

kjv: now will my husband dwell with me
mine: now my husband will honor me
note: The verb zabal is rare; related to zebul ("lofty abode") and Ugaritic zbl ("prince"), it is now usually taken as "exalt, honor", though "dwell with" (KJV, from zebul as dwelling) remains possible.
Hebrew nihashti is from nahash, the technical verb for divination or omen-reading (cf. 44:5, 15); "by experience" removes the reference to Laban's divining.

kjv: green poplar, and of the hazel and chesnut tree
mine: fresh rods of poplar and almond and plane trees
note: Hebrew livneh is the white poplar or storax, luz is the almond (as in the place name Luz), and armon is the oriental plane tree; hazel and chestnut are not native to the region.
